title: Sofia, 24: The '0% Interest' Laptop That Cost $472

scenes.say: $472 of interest, on a 0% deal. That's Sofia's new laptop.
She bought a $2,400 laptop on a store card. No interest for 12 months.
She paid $150 a month. Felt safe.
But $150 times 12 is only $1,800. $600 was still left on day 366.
That's the catch: deferred interest. Miss the deadline, and the whole year's interest lands at once.
At about 30% APR, that's roughly $472, added in one bill.
The fix was just $50 more a month. $200 times 12 clears it in time.
Got a 0% deal? Divide the price by the months. Subscribe so you don't make this mistake on your next paycheck, because 0% interest can turn into $472.

question: Have you ever had a '0% interest' deal turn into a surprise bill?
description: Sofia, 24, put a $2,400 laptop on a store card with 0% interest for 12 months and paid $150 a month. That left $600 at the deadline, and deferred interest at about 30% APR added roughly $472 at once. Paying $200 a month would have cleared it with no interest. Numbers are rounded US estimates; deferred-interest terms vary by card.
